reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about HEA diffusion, segregation, and oxidation behavior, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific, non-obvious mechanistic link between sluggish diffusion and protective oxide formation in HEAs.
premises: Sluggish diffusion is an intrinsic property of high-entropy alloys
Sluggish diffusion controls surface segregation of reactive elements (Cr, Al)
Controlled segregation leads to a dense, adherent, protective oxide scale
HEA oxidation kinetics are slower than conventional alloys with similar reactive content
The mechanism is general for HEAs with sufficient Cr and Al at high temperatures
